summary.one_liner: AIlice is an open-source, autonomous general-purpose AI agent that decomposes tasks across dynamically created sub-agents, meant to act as a local JARVIS-like assistant built on LLMs.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes AIlice as a multi-agent system built on an "Interactive Agents Call Tree" (IACT) architecture, where agents are created dynamically to break down tasks and can message their callers for more information. It provides a web dialogue interface launched via the `ailice` command, with optional voice dialogue (speech recognition and TTS). It supports commercial LLM APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Mistral, Groq, DeepSeek, OpenRouter) as well as local or self-hosted models through Hugging Face, LM Studio, and ollama via litellm. Extension modules run as separate processes and can be configured in config.json, and MCP servers can be wrapped with `ailice_mcp_wrapper`. Documented use cases include research, coding, system administration, literature review, and document generation. The README also says the project can run in Docker, with optional CUDA and GUI support.
use_cases: Autonomous research on a specialized topic
System administration tasks on a Linux machine
Literature review and reading academic papers
Running local LLMs as a private personal assistant
Connecting MCP tool servers to an agent
notable: Interactive Agents Call Tree architecture where sub-agents can pause and ask their caller for input
Interrupt button lets the user pause a running task and send guidance to the active agent
Per-agent model configuration via agentModelConfig, mixing local and commercial LLMs
Extension modules run as separate processes and the agent can build new ext-modules itself
caveats: README says local LLM use needs large hardware; only 70B+ models are said to perform tasks well (e.g., two RTX 4090s)
Windows support is limited; the README recommends Docker or WSL, and says Windows command execution tools are not integrated
Google search module is rate-limited by default; heavy use requires a Google Custom Search API key
Sharing feature (--share) was temporarily removed for security reasons
keywords: ask ai to write code and run it
